sentences: A significant portion of the film is taken up with onstage performances, including comic bits and toned-down striptease acts.
There is also a lot of backstage action not directly related to the evolving murder mystery but highlighting the characters and lifestyles of the performers and crew.
At a city burlesque theatre, performer the headliner (the stage name of the young woman) is becoming an audience favorite with her singing and striptease act.
Backstage she has mixed interactions with other performers, some of whom are catty and jealous while others are quite friendly, especially the friendly dancer.
Comic the funnyman tries to get friendly with her, but the headliner turns him away, not having had good experiences with comics before.
During a police raid on the theatre for violating "public decency" laws, the backstage lights go out, and someone tries to strangle the headliner but stops when a stagehand comes by.
A number of the performers and crew are thrown in jail but the theatre's owner and producer the impresario.
The impresario bails them out and awards each a share in the company to keep them with him.
A few nights later, another performer, the diva, is found strangled with a g-string after a violent argument with her boyfriend, gangster the mobster.

As a police investigation begins, the g-string believed to be the murder weapon goes missing and a number of possible suspects, both from the theatre and outside—including the headliner herself—come under suspicion.

The coroner, though, reveals that the diva's death was actually due to poison, and the funnyman reveals that he had hidden the g-string after someone had slipped it into his pocket, earning the headliner's appreciation.
The funnyman, however, is arrested but released when new evidence is discovered.
When the funnyman and the headliner are on stage for a comedy skit, the body of another rival, the exotic dancer, falls out of a prop; she has also been strangled with a g-string.
The murders and related events begin to tie up, and the police inspector, the lead investigator, recommends shutting down the theatre for safety.
The headliner, though, rallies the employees with a never-give-in speech, reminding them that they all now have ownership stakes in the company.
The headliner remains behind as everyone else leaves for the night.
The aged stagehand the old-timer appears, confesses to the murders and tries to strangle the headliner.
The police and the funnyman burst in and rescue her.
It transpires that the headliner and her friend the friendly dancer had decided to set a trap for the killer.
The funnyman fills in additional information, having discovered that the old-timer was actually the diva's grandfather, driven to an insane hatred of burlesque performers.
With all problems resolved, the funnyman proposes to the headliner and she accepts.
At a warehouse in the southern city, trucks are loaded with stacks of tires to be delivered to a northern city warehouse.
On a country road under cover of darkness, the tires are transferred to the racketeer (the actor.
The actor), an underworld figure and operator of a nightclub at the beach.
With the $50,000 earned from the transaction, the widow (the actress), who inherited the tire business from her late husband, plans to marry the crooner (the actor), a singer at the racketeer's café.
The two lovebirds head for the eastern city, but the crooner insists on stopping at an unoccupied cottage he notices from the road.
In the northern city private detective the gumshoe (the actor) succeeds in clearing actress the starlet (the actress) of a murder charge and becomes a media sensation.
After the trial is over, the gumshoe rushes to phone his sweetheart, the girlfriend (the actress), a real estate agent at the shore.
The girlfriend, jealous of the starlet, is upset when the gumshoe informs her that he plans to shield the starlet from the reporters by hiding her at his beach cottage.
The newsman (the actor), a reporter and a rival for the girlfriend's affections, convinces her to play a practical joke.
They take a wax model to the gumshoe's cottage and stick a knife in the figure's throat.
The gumshoe and the starlet arrive at the cottage and are horrified to find blood stains and a body of a woman in the cellar.
Hurrying to the racketeer's café nearby, they telephone the police captain (the actor.
The actor) at police headquarters.
When the officers arrive, accompanied by the newsman and the girlfriend, the body is missing and the dummy lies in its place.
Believing that it is all a publicity hoax, the police ridicule the gumshoe as a "front page detective."
After the police leave, the girlfriend admits her involvement in placing the dummy and offers to help the gumshoe discover the identity of the murdered woman.
A dress label found on the body leads them to an exclusive shop in the southern city, where they discover that the dress was sold to the widow.
After an argument, the gumshoe and the girlfriend go their separate ways to solve the mystery.
Upon learning that the widow left town to marry the crooner, their investigation leads to the racketeer's café.
The girlfriend begins to question the crooner about the widow, whereupon he flees the café with the $50,000.
His escape is aided by the sound of air raid sirens and a blackout at the beach.
By pretending to be an air raid warden, the gumshoe corners the crooner at his apartment.

After the crooner denies killing the widow and accuses the racketeer of engineering the murder and hijacking the tires, the gumshoe phones the police captain, but before he can relay the information, the crooner knocks him unconscious and locks him in a closet.
The crooner is then confronted by the racketeer and his henchman, the thug (the actor), who have followed him.
When the police arrive, they find the crooner's body, beaten to death, and accuse the gumshoe of the crime.
After recovering from a blow to his head, the gumshoe eludes the police and goes to the café, where he confronts the racketeer and the thug with evidence of murder.
In the ensuing fight, the thug and the racketeer chase the gumshoe into a banquet room where the hijacked tires are stored.
The police then arrive and, seizing the tires as evidence, arrest the racketeer and the thug.
With the murder solved, the gumshoe and the girlfriend leave for their wedding and honeymoon.
Former jewel thief and reformed detective the adventurer, or the gentleman rogue, is driving to a party with his butler the manservant.
Halfway through the journey, they come across the socialite, who requests that they take her to the swindler's residence.
Meanwhile, the swindler, an unprofessed criminal, is carrying out a scheme to loot the jewelry of select wealthy persons — namely, the first wealthy woman, the second wealthy woman and the socialite.
The swindler is killed before he can finish his plans by an unknown assailant.
The adventurer, who happens to be at the scene, is pinpointed by the suspicious police as the perpetrator.
He escapes but is found by magazine writer the journalist, who agrees not to rat the adventurer out in exchange for a scoop.
The gentleman rogue interrogates the women at the murder scene but is unable to find a lead.
He is then captured by two criminals working under the henchman, the swindler's right-hand man.
The adventurer breaks free and flees, reuniting with the manservant and the journalist.
The trio sneak into the swindler's house and decide to tail the henchman, who is leaving for the airport.
The criminal turns out to be meeting a teenager named the girl.
Unaware of the swindler's death, she becomes distressed when the news is broken to her.
The henchman and the girl later leave for a hotel.
In the middle of his confidence trick on the girl, the henchman is halted by the adventurer, the manservant, and the journalist, who rush into the hotel room.
A heated fight ensues, with the henchman managing to escape.
The girl injures herself and is quickly attended to by the journalist.
When she admits her love for the swindler, the journalist is infuriated.
The adventurer realizes that the girl is the journalist's spouse and by piecing two and two together, he concludes that the journalist was the swindler's killer.
The police arrive in time to arrest the jealous lover, and the gentleman rogue is exonerated.
The adventurer, the gentleman rogue, agrees to go to the port city to help the allied cause during the world war.
There, he and his valet, the manservant, are met by his old friend, nightclub owner the proprietor.
The chauffeur comes to drive him, supposedly to see the intelligence chief, head of the British secret service in the region.
However, he is actually taken to meet the spy chief, the leader of an enemy spy ring.
The spy chief threatens to kill the manservant (whom he has kidnapped) unless the adventurer does some as yet unspecified work for him.
When the adventurer reluctantly agrees, the two men are released.
After they leave, the spy chief reveals to the chauffeur that he expects the gentleman rogue to try to trap him, but that is all part of his plan.

When the adventurer meets with the intelligence chief, the spymaster makes clear that he does not want an amateur's help, but reluctantly agrees to let the gentleman rogue play along in order to gather more information.

Complicating matters further, the adventurer and the manservant encounter the latter's son the young man, a British naval officer, and his fiancée, reporter the newswoman in the proprietor's nightclub.
The adventurer soon suspects that she is not all she appears to be.

In the proprietor's private office, he also re-encounters freelance spy or informant "the first freelancer" and meets a new one calling himself "the second freelancer" (both more or less on friendly terms with the proprietor).
The second freelancer shows him that the lace the newswoman was knitting contains a secret message.
When the two spies leave, the first freelancer shoots the second freelancer; he dies in front of the nightclub, at the newswoman's feet.
When the newswoman returns to her hotel room, the spy chief is waiting for her.
She is one of his agents, currently extracting information from the young man for their real goal: the plans for the minefields and defences of the canal.
Meanwhile, the gentleman rogue is approached by "the third freelancer", yet another unscrupulous man with information to sell.
The third freelancer sells him the lace that the newswoman had sent to a laundry; the hidden message indicates that whatever the enemy plan to do is to be finished by midnight.
The spy chief gives the adventurer his assignment: break into a safe at the intelligence headquarters and steal some documents.
However, it eventually becomes clear to all that the adventurer's part is merely a distraction.
The plans have already been stolen.
The intelligence chief orders the arrest of the gentleman rogue for treason, but the adventurer escapes.
He and the manservant head for the laundry.
Along the way, they come upon the unconscious young man.
They revive him and take him along.
Inside, they find secret rooms and overpower the chauffeur.
They also discover the body of the third freelancer and a clue, shards of a distinctive watch crystal, just like the one the newswoman has, microfilming equipment, and ashes of the defence plans.
The adventurer deduces that the plans have been copied to the newswoman's watch crystal.
When she telephones, the adventurer pretends to be the spy chief and learns that she is at the hotel.
Before they get there, however, the first freelancer kills her and takes the watch to the spy chief.
Fortunately, the proprietor has access to a biplane armed with machine guns.
The adventurer pilots it, finds the speeding car taking the spy chief and the first freelancer to the submarine, and strafes them.
The car crashes, putting the spy chief and the first freelancer out of commission, possibly dead, and the watch smashed.

The detective postpones his trip home from service with the government to the island city to help with the investigation of murder involving his eldest daughter (the actress) and an easily spooked chauffeur (the actor).
The victim is murdered in the middle of a seance with a total of 8 witnesses, seen and unseen, present.
The detective's daughter the young woman (real name the detective's surname) is one of the witnesses and is detained.
When police learn of the young woman's true identity as the detective's daughter, he is summoned to police headquarters.
The police offer the case to the famous Chinese Detective and he reluctantly agrees in order to get his daughter released.
The police cannot find a gun anywhere in the house.
Police then learn from the coroner that the victim was shot and the bullet did not go all the way thorough, yet it is not lodged anywhere in the body.
The seance room is supported by a gadget room to assist in the various ghostly appearances.
The chauffeur's comedy with the various seance gadgets serve to link the movie audience with a "me too" bond which is very warm and human.
Since there was no gun and no bullet, the detective has the Coroner perform an experiment to determine what might have happened.
The case is solved when the murderer brushes up against the detective in a reenactment of the crime with the detective sitting where the murdered man was sitting.
The investigator, known to the police as the "amateur detective" the gentleman adventurer, is enjoying his vacation at the racetrack.
There he meets an old nemesis, paroled mobster the ex-convict -- the gentleman adventurer's testimony in court convicted him.
The local police inspector greets the gentleman adventurer suspiciously, and two strange women impose upon the suave sleuth, resulting in one stealing a purse from the other.
The gentleman adventurer hails a cab, driven by devil-may-care the cabbie, and follows the thief to the film studio movie lot.
The cabbie also works in the film industry as a stunt driver, and is already familiar with the studio layout.
Hearing a gunshot, the gentleman adventurer rushes to a deserted sound stage, where he finds a corpse; when he summons a studio guard, the body has disappeared.

The sleuth, accompanied by the cabbie, pokes around the studio and finds various clues in unusual hiding places, including the missing corpse: the actor, the leading man in the studio's major production, supervised by neurotic studio executive the mogul.

The suspects are struggling starlet the ingenue, haughty prima donna the diva, the gangster the ex-convict, autocratic director the filmmaker, costume designer the dressmaker (once married to the deceased), and the producer the mogul.
The gentleman adventurer deduces plausible motives for these suspicious characters, and even confronts each of them with his revelations.
After the death of the leading man, one disaster after another befalls the jinxed movie production, to the beleaguered producer's agony.
The gentleman adventurer, knowing that someone is sabotaging the production, finds an important clue.
Interpreting the clue correctly, the sleuth confronts the saboteur, who races desperately into a darkened sound stage and tries to escape in the catwalks high above the stage.
The gentleman adventurer risks his life but solves the case.
The detective, aka the sleuth, helps the mysterious woman enter an art gallery late at night to supposedly recover a painting that belongs to her.
The sleuth discovers that the woman is the model for the artist's painting.
However, the artist, the painter has been dead for 15 years.
The owner of the gallery lies murdered on the floor.

When the security guards arrive, alerted by a burglar alarm, they try to arrest the detective but he escapes with the painting and goes to the home of the millionaire, a collector of the painter's work.
Wanted by the American police for murder, the sleuth finds the girl, the late artist's daughter, and they travel to the capital city.
At the airport, the girl is met by a car from the lakeside inn and slips away.
After she drives away, the detective hires taxi driver the local man and his son, the boy, to follow her.
The lakeside inn is located in a country village was where her father lived and worked.

The girl introduces the detective to her stepmother the widow, a dancer, and the widow's partner and new husband the male dancer, who warns the detective to leave the girl alone and get out of the country.
At the inn, desk clerk the receptionist shows the painter's studio, where the detective finds a drawing done in the painter's style, with its paint still wet.
The mysterious woman, searching for her portrait in the detective's room, is surprised by his early return, but when he pursues her into the hallway, she makes her getaway.
When he returns to his room, an unknown assailant knocks him unconscious and steals the painting.
The mysterious woman's father searches for his daughter, but when her body turns up drowned in the lake, the detective thinks she has been murdered.
The millionaire arrives at the hotel without his famous diamond ring, a piece of jewelry he always wears.
At dinner the girl collapses, the victim of poisoning, leaving the detective with a puzzling mystery that may be linked to the disappearance of the painter.
If the painter is still alive, who stands to gain from that?
At the lake, the detective finds the receptionist, dead in a boat.
The local man appears and reveals that he is an undercover Mexican police officer, who also needs to find the killer on the loose.
Back at the inn, they discover the girl is missing and on her way to an island, where her father's grave is located.
They locate her, seated in front of her father's crypt and wall headstone, accompanied by a woman.
When the detective removes the headstone, however, he sees that the crypt is empty.
The woman standing by the girl tries to sidle away unnoticed, but the rest question her and find out she was paid to take the girl to see her father's crypt and knows nothing else.
After a performance of the traditional dance (the dance of the old men), a man dressed with an old man's mask, similar to the other dancers, approaches the girl and reveals himself to be her father.
He explains that his disappearance came about when his alleged suicide made his paintings valuable.
As the painter warns the girl that their lives are in danger, he is shot dead.
The detective deduces that the killer must be the millionaire, and he sets a trap for him.
Wearing the painter's disguise, the detective walks onto the plaza with the girl by his side.
Just before the millionaire can shoot from a balcony, the local man fires.
With the killer brought to justice, the detective is given a dark-colored, engraved leather case from the local man, who says his son, the boy, bought it for the detective.
He calls it a 'memorandum' instead of a memento, and then the detective bids farewell to his Mexican friends to board a plane bound for home.
Successful attorney the husband neglects his wife, the woman, so she leaves him.
The husband tries to win her back, but finds that she is now dating the painter, an artist.
The painter's girlfriend, jealous and upset that boyfriend the painter is stepping out on her, intends to shoot him in his apartment.
The husband, who is there to confront the painter, wrestles away the gun, which goes off and kills her.
An eyewitness mistakes the husband in a dark hallway for the painter, who is arrested and charged with the crime.
The woman pleads with the husband to defend the painter in court.
As the trial proceeds, witnesses begin to realize that it was the husband, the attorney, and not the defendant who was in the hallway that night.
He even shows that a pair of the painter's gloves fit himself.
The gloves fit, the jury acquits, and the woman, realizing how clever her husband is, returns to him.
Eight people, all strangers to each other, are invited to a small isolated island off the coast of a southern county, the country, by a host and hostess.
They settle in at a mansion tended by two newly hired servants, the butler and his wife (a married couple), but their hosts are absent.
When the guests sit down to dinner, they notice the centerpiece, ten figurines of Indians.

The butler puts on a gramophone record, through which a man's voice accuses them all of murder: the general – ordering his wife's lover, a lieutenant under his command, to his death the spinster – the death of her young nephew the doctor.
The doctor – drunkenness which resulted in a patient dying the prince – killing a couple while speeding in a car the young woman – murdering her sister's fiancé the judge.
The judge – being responsible for the hanging of an innocent man the adventurer – causing the deaths of 21 South African tribesmen the private detective.

The private detective – perjury, resulting in an innocent man's death the butler and his wife – the demise of their previous employer, an invalid It becomes apparent that none of them knows or has even seen the host.
The host and they realize the name stands for "unknown."
They also cannot leave the island, as the butler informs them that the boat will not return until Monday, and it is only Friday.
The prince admits his guilt, then dies after his drink is poisoned.
The next morning, it is discovered that the butler's wife died in her sleep.
The guests notice that one figurine is broken and another missing and with the two deaths matching the old nursery rhyme, they search the island for "the host" without success.
After the general is stabbed to death, the judge declares that the host must be one of them.
They vote on who they suspect the host is; as the only person to get more than one vote, the butler is made to sleep in the woodshed.
The next morning, they find him dead, his head split open with an axe.
The spinster dies next, her body found with a hypodermic needle nearby.
The doctor discovers that his needle is missing, as is the adventurer's revolver.
At dinner, the judge, the doctor, the private detective and the adventurer all confess to their crimes.
When it is the young woman's turn, she excuses herself to get her coat and the others hear her shriek and rush to her.
In the confusion, a single gunshot is heard.
They find her shaken after being brushed by seaweed hanging from the ceiling.
They also find the adventurer's gun, with the judge dead from a shot to the head.
The young woman insists she is innocent, but the doctor suspects her and locks her in her room.
That night, the young woman admits to the adventurer that her sister killed her own fiancé, and that the young woman helped her cover up the crime and took the blame.
The two later realize the doctor is missing.
The next morning, the private detective is struck by stonework toppled from the floor above.
The adventurer sees a corpse on the beach, which turns out to be the doctor.
The young woman holds the adventurer's gun against him, certain that he must be the killer.
He tells her that his real name is a different one, and that the real adventurer was his friend who committed suicide.
The impostor urges her to shoot but deliberately miss him – he then drops as if shot.
She returns to the house and finds a noose hanging in the parlor and discovers that the judge, who is very much alive, is the mysterious host.
The judge tells her that all his life he had searched for perfect justice.
After learning that he was terminally ill, he concocted this plan.
He persuaded the doctor to help him fake his own death, then murdered him.
He tells her that she can either hang herself or be sent to the gallows (as the only possible perpetrator).
He then drinks poisoned whiskey, while the impostor appears behind him, alive and well.
The judge dies and the boat arrives, rescuing the impostor and the young woman.
The reformed thief's wealthy friend, the millionaire, purchases an upscale bookstore from aged the bookseller, but retains his services as a book expert.
However, when the bookseller becomes ill just before an important auction he was to conduct, the reformed thief proves that he can impersonate him, fooling everyone, including the police inspector.
With the assistance of store employee the saleswoman, the reformed thief runs the auction without a hitch.
The centerpiece is a rare first edition of a famous novelist's classic novel, which goes for $62,000.
However, the purchaser discovers that the book is a fake and demands his money back. $50,000 had already been sent to the book's owner/forger, the swindler.
The reformed thief tracks him down, but arrives just too late.
The swindler's partner, the saleswoman, finds him packed and ready to leave.
She shoots him and takes the money.
The reformed thief hears the gunfire, forcing her to flee; in her haste, the money gets stuck in the other doorway.
The reformed thief takes the envelope of cash.
By sheer bad timing, the police inspector and the sergeant arrive while the reformed thief is examining the swindler's body, and arrest him for murder.
The reformed thief has little difficulty escaping.
Still unaware of the identity of the real murderer, he takes the saleswoman into his confidence.
He puts the money in the store's safe while she watches with interest.
That night, she and her husband, escaped safecracker the convict, break into the shop, but are forced to leave without the cash when the reformed thief and the millionaire arrive.
When the convict arranges to meet the reformed thief, the reformed thief recognizes him.

He agrees to give the convict half the proceeds, but the reformed thief's sidekick "the little fellow" informs the saleswoman that he will not be bringing real cash, and that the $50,000 is stashed in the millionaire's home safe.
The convict and an accomplice tie the reformed thief up.
The convict then leaves to get the money.
The reformed thief gets free, phones the police inspector and heads to the millionaire's suite.
There, he and the little fellow capture and bind the convict.

Then the reformed thief forces the saleswoman to write out a confession, convincing her how coldblooded he can be by pretending to shoot her husband dead (the unseen little fellow just knocks him out).
The convict regains consciousness and control of the situation, allowing the saleswoman to burn her confession.
When the police inspector and his men break in, the reformed thief presents the inspector with a blank sheet of paper, claiming he switched the pages.
The saleswoman incriminates herself and is arrested and taken away with her husband, the convict.
